title: Stage 5: Refresh tokens
summary: Long sessions without long-lived access tokens: opaque, hashed refresh tokens with rotation, reuse detection and logout.

steps.title: Stage 5: refresh
body: - `POST /login` also returns `refresh_token`: an opaque random value (32 random bytes as hex, **not** a JWT), stored only as a SHA-256 hash, valid 14 days, starting a new **family**.

- `POST /refresh {"refreshToken": "..."}`: a live, unused token gets a new access token **and** a new refresh token in the same family; the old one is marked used. Unknown, expired or revoked -> `401`. A token that was **already used** -> revoke its whole family and `401`.
- `POST /logout {"refreshToken": "..."}`: revoke that token's family, `204` (also `204` for unknown tokens).
`/refresh` issues the access token from the **current** user record, so a role change takes effect at the next refresh.

steps.prompt: Why is the refresh token opaque and looked up in a store, while the access token is a self-contained JWT?
options: Refresh tokens must be revocable instantly and are used rarely, so a lookup is cheap; access tokens are checked on every request
JWTs can't be longer than 15 minutes
So the client can read the refresh token's claims

lines: hash the presented token and look it up; unknown -> null
if its family is revoked -> null
if it was already used -> revoke the family, null
mark it used and issue a new token in the same family
also: hash the presented token and look it up; unknown -> null

steps.title: Rotation, reuse detection, logout
prompt: Finish the API. **Run checks** starts your server and runs every stage's tests plus the refresh flow.

Suggested: a `class RefreshTokenStore` with `Issue(user, family, now)`, `Rotate(token, now)` returning `(string Token, string User)?`, and `RevokeFamilyOf(token)`, using a lock around `Rotate` so two parallel refreshes can't both succeed.

static class T
public static string B64(byte[] d) => Convert.ToBase64String(d).TrimEnd('=').Replace('+', '-').Replace('/', '_');
public static string B64(string s) => B64(System.Text.Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(s));
public static readonly byte[] Key = System.Text.Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes("secure-the-api-signing-key-0123456789");
public static string Sign(string payload, byte[]? key = null)
var input = B64("{\"alg\":\"HS256\",\"typ\":\"JWT\"}") + "." + B64(payload);
return input + "." + B64(System.Security.Cryptography.HMACSHA256.HashData(key ?? Key, System.Text.Encoding.ASCII.GetBytes(input)));
public static string For(string sub, string role = "user", long exp = 4102444800, string aud = "secure-api") =>
public static JsonElement Payload(string? jwt)
var p = (jwt ?? "").Split('.');
if (p.Length != 3) return default;
var s = p[1].Replace('-', '+').Replace('_', '/');
try { return JsonDocument.Parse(Convert.FromBase64String(s.PadRight(s.Length + (4 - s.Length % 4) % 4, '='))).RootElement; }
catch { return default; }
public static bool Signed(string? jwt)
var p = (jwt ?? "").Split('.');
return p.Length == 3 && B64(System.Security.Cryptography.HMACSHA256.HashData(Key, System.Text.Encoding.ASCII.GetBytes(p[0] + "." + p[1]))) == p[2];
public static Task<HttpResponseMessage> Post(HttpClient http, string url, object body) => http.PostAsJsonAsync(url, body);
public static Task<HttpResponseMessage> Send(HttpClient http, HttpMethod m, string url, string? token, object? body = null)
var msg = new HttpRequestMessage(m, url);
if (token is not null) msg.Headers.TryAddWithoutValidation("Authorization", "Bearer " + token);
if (body is not null) msg.Content = JsonContent.Create(body);
return http.SendAsync(msg);
public static async Task<JsonElement> Login(HttpClient http, string user, string password) =>
await DojoWeb.Json(await http.PostAsJsonAsync("/login", new { username = user, password }));
